card.title: 113. SCHÜTZEN
card.flavorText: The 113th Schützen-Regiment (riflemen regiment in English) was a unit belonging to the 1st Panzer Division of the German Wehrmacht during WWII. It was renamed 113th Panzergrenadier-Regiment in 1941. The division participated in the annexation of Austria and the occupation of the Sudetenland in 1938. In 1939, it took part in the invasions of Czechoslovakia and Poland. In 1940, the 1st Panzer Division fought in the Battle of France, seeing combat in Sedan and Dunkirk, and later it participated in the assault on the Weygand Line in northern France. In June 1941, the division joined Operation Barbarossa as part of Army Group North, engaging in intense fighting during the advance towards Leningrad. By October 1941, it was reassigned to Army Group Center to support the advance on Moscow, reaching within 32 km of the city before retreating due to Soviet counterattacks. Throughout the winter of 1942–43, the division participated in defensive operations on the Eastern Front, suffering heavy losses, until it was eventually sent to France for refitting. After an uneventful period in France and later in Greece, the 1st Panzer Division returned to the Eastern Front, where it fought in Kiev, Zhitomir, and Cherkassy. Severely weakened by March 1944, it retreated west, engaging in Poland and Hungary, including an unsuccessful attempt to relieve Budapest. In May 1945, the division surrendered to US forces in southern Bavaria, avoiding Soviet capture.
